kept.spine: A stranger arriving in Hochhausen finds the market without asking the way, since the road that carries the town's traffic runs straight to it.
Order here is professional and paid for: Hochhausen trusts neither luck nor its neighbours for its safety.
Nothing Hochhausen needs goes long unfound, and nothing it makes goes long unsold.
More grievances get opened in Hochhausen than get closed.
A careful eye passing through Hochhausen notices first that nothing here is spare.
Magic is not practised in Hochhausen, nor arranged for, nor expected.
From its own harvest Hochhausen feeds itself, proof against a closed road and not against a poor one.
A day spent in Hochhausen would not show that The Commercial Circle and The Administrative Circle are at odds. It surfaces only on the second day.
Goods move into Hochhausen and out of it, and neither direction draws any notice.
A road carries Hochhausen's trade: goods arrive, goods leave, and people pass through.
Hochhausen has settled at the size a village of its kind settles at, and it has stayed there.
One tie in Hochhausen carries more weight than the rest, and that weight shows in what the town does and does not do.
The people of Hochhausen are connected the way people in any settled place are connected, and there is nothing more notable to say of it.
A loose end is there for a careful reader of Hochhausen to find, the kind a single institution could tie off.
